summary.headline: Paytm's Q2 FY27: two quarters of 28% growth; 2.5 bps UPI MDR could add about ₹700 crore EBITDA at current GMV.
summary.overview: Management described Q2 FY27 as a strong quarter, with reported growth of 28% for two consecutive quarters and about 30%+ excluding the prior-year PIDF effect. Payments GMV was roughly flat QoQ, which management attributed to seasonality (late Diwali) and to walking away from unprofitable large merchant contracts. The call centred on the UPI MDR framework (which was postponed from 15 October to post-Diwali), the AI-led merchant platform, and the DLG accounting change with one lending partner. Management said MDR is upside to the model and not factored into its base plan. Cloud/AI costs rose, with management attributing the increase to a one-time consolidation of online and offline payment stacks plus ongoing AI spend.

segments.name: Payments (UPI and P2M)
segments.commentary: P2M GMV was flat QoQ, which management linked to Q2 seasonality and to exiting a large low-contribution enterprise contract. Management expects GMV growth and market-share gains ahead of MDR.

segments.name: Lending (merchant, personal, DLG)
segments.commentary: Management said lending is growing well across the board and that personal loans are in a tailwind. The DLG change means one lender's DLG is being charged upfront at the start of the quarter, which is a drag on contribution in the quarter in which the DLG is given. Management said no impact in Q2.

segments.name: Financial services distribution and marketing services
segments.commentary: Management said the marketing services business has recovered and that AI-driven merchant service revenue will be booked in marketing services. Management guided that this would take two to three more quarters to become meaningful.

segments.name: Paytm Cloud Technologies Ltd (PCTL)
segments.commentary: A 100% subsidiary used as a vehicle for overseas ventures (UAE, Luxembourg). PAT rose about 7x YoY to ₹84 crore, per the analyst's figure.

guidance_outlook: UPI MDR at 2.5 bps: management said it would be bottom-line accretive and is not in the base plan. The framework is a 40 bps cap, with a switch-on on day one and no merchant negotiation.
MDR implementation was postponed from 15 October to post-Diwali. Management said the framework is final and it is ready to implement, but NPCI controls the date.
Indirect expense growth is expected to normalise after the one-time migration and AI spend, with a longer-term aim of revenue growing faster than indirect costs.
Management said it targets operating leverage (revenue or CM growing faster than indirect costs) and expects free cash flow to improve, with more capex guidance to come.
Management will not report adjusted EBITDA; EBITDA is stated after ESOP costs.
capex_capacity: Device capex of about ₹400 crore on an inward device count basis; management said it is a little higher than before, linked to focusing on engagement and retention.
Up to ₹500 crore enabling resolution for PCTL over 12 months in multiple tranches. No firm deployment plan; management said any investment would be approved by the board and disclosed if material.
AI-driven merchant platform (credit, insurance, wealth, AI agents) is being built with subscription and transaction fee models; no launch date given, with monetisation expected within about a year.
demand_pricing: UPI MDR framework: 40 bps cap, flip-switch implementation for small merchants; management said MDR is applicable to transactions above ₹2,000 and is not factored into the company's base plan.
Net payment margin (ex-UPI) moved from about 8.5 bps to about 9 bps, attributed to pricing discipline, share gains, and EMI, DCC and enterprise products.
Management said it is seeing tailwinds across 85–90% of the business and only small headwinds in equity broking (weak market volumes) and travel, with some wealth weakness.
Management said consumer market share is the primary KPI, with monthly transacting users (MTU) growth driven by better acquisition targeting rather than spend.
Management said a large insurance-company contract was concluded, reducing GMV but improving bottom-line contribution.

qa_highlights.question: How will the 2.5 bps UPI MDR flow to EBITDA, and is the company scaling up consumer acquisition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it bottom-line accretive and not part of the base plan. Madhur Deora said 2.5 bps on ₹28 lakh crore GMV gives about ₹700 crore at current scale, roughly ₹900 crore at FY28 numbers, and the company will stay aggressive on consumer acquisition.

qa_highlights.question: Will the MDR be implemented in December, and is industry readiness adequate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the industry and its systems are ready and that the timing decision lies with NPCI. Management said the company is a participant and does not decide the date.

qa_highlights.question: Is the DLG versus non-DLG mix changing, and what is the accounting?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company does not manage the DLG mix and works with any lender, DLG or no DLG. DLG is charged upfront at the start of the arrangement (conservative accounting). One lender's DLG returned after six quarters, and management flagged it early; there is no impact in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Why was P2M GMV flat QoQ, and does this reflect a pricing choice?
qa_highlights.answer: Madhur Deora said Q2 is seasonally softer than Q1, and late Diwali pushes the festive season into Q3. Management also said it let go of a large contract that was not meeting its contribution threshold, which was a meaningful but not double-digit share of GMV.

qa_highlights.question: Is the indirect expense spike in software and cloud a one-off, and what is the AI drag?
qa_highlights.answer: Madhur Deora said the cloud increase reflects a one-time consolidation of two payment stacks (online and offline) and ongoing AI spend. Vijay Shekhar Sharma said AI has no drag on P&L, because savings or revenue offset the spend.

qa_highlights.question: What is the risk profile of the lending book, and what is the ECL trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Madhur Deora said merchant loan ECL is largely unchanged, personal loans are mainly ECL-reserved, and the company is not loosening underwriting. Vijay Shekhar Sharma said the company does not sell insurance and that the book is owned by partner lenders.

risks_watch: UPI MDR timing (post-Diwali, NPCI-controlled) and competitive pass-through to merchants, especially the top 2–5% of spenders who pay on transactions above ₹2,000.
DLG accounting: upfront charge in the quarter a DLG is given, which can drag contribution and EBITDA; the mix can change quarter to quarter.
Cloud and AI cost trajectory after the one-time migration; indirect expense growth versus revenue growth.
Seasonality of P2M GMV, and the quality versus quantity trade-off as Paytm exits low-contribution contracts.
Lending book quality as merchant and personal loan scale grows; monitor ECL and collections data.
PCTL overseas investments of up to ₹500 crore over 12 months.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on MDR, lending, and AI, with a notable willingness to flag accounting timing (DLG) early. Management was evasive on the NPCI date and on the operational and competitive detail behind the MDR outcome, and it declined to quantify the external competitive factor.
key_quotes: Yeah, so on our GMV, which is 28 lakh crores, at a current scale, 2.5 bps would give you slightly over 700 crores.
We don't say no to a lender just because they want DLG.
It's zero drag. There is migration of the cloud from other payment systems to the new system.

adds.what: Device rollout ~700,000 devices in quarter (device capex ~₹400 crore on inward device count basis, not a capacity addition with a stated size)
AI-driven merchant platform (credit, insurance, wealth, AI agents) - no launch date given; monetisation expected within about a year

growth.why: Management cites two consecutive quarters of 28% reported revenue growth (30%+ ex-PIDF base) and tailwinds across 85-90% of the business, with net payment margin up from ~8.5 to ~9 bps; the UPI MDR upside (~₹700 crore at 2.5 bps) is explicitly outside the base plan and its date depends on NPCI, so backing is partial.
